rewrites.summary:
This Land hosts the flashpoint of the country's 2026 prison-placement controversy: the July 2026 ruling and transfer that sent a prisoner whose legal gender had been changed under the federal Self-Determination Act to a men's prison issued from the regional court at Neubrandenburg (corroborated by multiple reports, 15-17 July 2026). The same case drove three other Länder to launch a Bundesrat initiative to tighten that Act — a framework-level event whose consequences bind prison administration, a Land competence, everywhere.

Otherwise the surviving record shows no Land-specific trans statute, placement reform, ordinance or event-security finding: a March 2026 constitutional-law survey of the 2023-26 wave of Land prison-placement reforms (placing inmates per the civil-register entry) names other Länder as reformers, not this one. Visitor exposure tracks the national framework; the placement rules bear on detained people.

rewrites.summary:
Rhineland-Palatinate replaced its prison-execution code with a new § 17, in force 1 March 2026, anchoring inmate placement to the civil-register sex entry — the first reform of the wave that, per a March 2026 constitutional-law survey, made such registry-based placement the majority practice among the Länder. The same essay, written against the July 2026 case in which a prisoner whose legal gender had been changed under the federal Self-Determination Act was sent to a men's prison, argues the registry standard is constitutionally avoidable and some Land versions doubtful, defending inclusive pre-correction placement as constitutional.

These are detained-person rules in a field that is a Land competence; no other Rhineland-Palatine trans statute, ordinance, enforcement series or event-security finding survives in the records, so visitor exposure tracks the national framework.

rewrites.summary:
Spain's Law 4/2023 for the real and effective equality of trans people (official gazette text) vests implementation of its administrative and education-facing provisions in the autonomous communities — this region's government among them. The parallel 2023 gender-recognition reform, letting registry entries change by self-declaration from age 12 without medical diagnosis, drew an international rights organisation to rank the country among autonomy-first jurisdictions.

The surviving record adds no Galician statute, ordinance, enforcement series or incident finding; regional value here is implementation posture under the 2023 framework, not separate restriction or separate protection.

No Chaco-specific trans statute, quota-compliance finding or enforcement series survives in the record. The framework is national: a April 2025 national feature described the trans community facing a 'chaotic, desperate situation' after decree roll-back of the Gender Identity Law, and a national hate-crime observatory reported 227 SOGI-motivated hate crimes for 2025 — up 62% year-on-year, its highest decade count, one every 38 hours, most attackers security-force personnel or unidentified — a baseline applying across the provinces including this one.

Visitor exposure in Chaco therefore tracks the national position: no provincial criminalisation survives in the record, amid a documented national surge in anti-trans violence and a contested federal law.
